$description: Shared physics: type roles, scale, line-height, tracking, optical-size ratio and ink floors. Delivery (self-hosted files, subset or fallback path) is decided per target.

display.$description: Default only; every world overrides world.type.display.family with a face of its own character.

reading.$description: Reading voice for sustained prose; proportional, never mono. The web fallback matches measured upright advances and the delivered face's 970/250 ascent/descent per 1000 units. It only applies while the designed face loads or is unavailable.

system.$description: System voice, machine-oriented: commands, navigation and control labels where they are addresses or commands, metadata, timestamps, identifiers, paths, keys, command results and machine state. Never reading prose; never display by default.

code.$description: Code and literal input: the system face, in its own role so a target can deliver a distinct code face without touching the system voice.

numeric.$description: Default numeric voice: tabular figures with units attached. Worlds choose theirs through world.type.numeric.family; type.numeric.width applies only where that face has a width axis.

display.$description: Base display weight; worlds override through world.type.display.weight.

block-size.$description: Code blocks use a compact mono size while retaining the system face's full reading weight.

inline-scale.$description: Inline code follows its surrounding text's x-height: Instrument Sans 510 units to Martian Mono 600 units, with the shared minimum size retained.

width.$description: Width-axis value (wdth) for tabular figures in a face with a width axis; no effect otherwise.

body.$description: Operational text: forms, lists, controls, captions.

micro.$description: Floor. No text below 12px; small never means faint.

display-fluid.$description: Fluid display step: a rem min and a max at least double it.

quote.$description: Compact quotation leading within an attributed fan card.

tracking.$description: Letter-spacing in em (numbers: DTCG dimensions allow only px/rem; CSS output appends the unit).

system.$description: Uppercase and system labels; ledger range .06–.12em.

ratio.$description: Authored optical-size multiplier for renderers that map text size to a supported opsz axis; browser auto sizing is independent.

card-title.$description: Subordinate title of an optical scene invitation.

card-body.$description: Short supporting copy within an optical scene invitation.

premise.$description: Brief reading ground beside a cinematic statement.

line-height.$description: Leading for compact cinematic premises and invitations.

headline-fluid.$description: Viewport fraction setting the field statement.

headline-leading.$description: Tight leading of a large optical field statement.

headline-tracking.$description: Em tracking of the optical field statement.

note.$description: Readable annotation accompanying a field statement.

closer-min.$description: Quiet closing question in the handheld field.

closer-max.$description: Quiet closing question in the wide field.

closer-fluid.$description: Viewport fraction setting the field closing question.

headline-mobile.$description: Handheld editorial opening title and subordinate premise.

secondary-weight.$description: Subordinate premise weight against its primary title.

detail.$description: Compact readable supporting prose over an ambient opening.

caption.$description: Editorial programme caption and compact navigation.

title-stacked.$description: Measured process stage heading in the stacked composition; keeps the ordinal with the title on narrow reading surfaces.

headline-fluid.$description: Opening heading size as a viewport-width fraction.

headline-leading.$description: Leading of the large central opening heading.

headline-tracking.$description: Letter spacing of the opening heading in em units.

ink.$description: Ink opacity ladder over the world's ink colour. Floors, not styles.

system.$description: Floor for system/metadata text. Never lower for anything that must be read.

recessive.$description: Reading apparatus at rest on quiet pages; returns to the system floor on hover, focus or proximity. Not for content that must be read at rest.
